To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a deep CNN trained on a large dataset can classify skin cancer at the level of board-certified dermatologists.

(1) we have trained a deep neural network to classify skin lesions using a dataset of clinical images that is two orders of magnitude more images than previous studies, and (2) we show that this deep learning approach can achieve performance on par with board certified dermatologists in two binary classification tasks, one for identifying the most common cancers and the other for identifying the deadliest skin cancer

a deep convolutional neural network can classify skin cancer as well as board certified dermatologists, and that a deep neural network can be used to identify the most common cancers as well as the deadliest skin cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a diagnostic tool for the classification of skin cancer using deep neural networks.
a fundamental question: Can a computer see as well as a doctor?
the question of whether artificial intelligence is capable of classifying the skin with a level of competency comparable to dermatologists
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a deep convolutional neural network, trained on a large dataset of clinical images, can be used to diagnose skin cancer at least as accurately as board-certified dermatologists.
the results presented in this paper are the first to show a deep convolutional neural network capable of performing a dermatologist level classification of the most deadly skin cancers.
the CNN achieves performance comparable to the dermatologists, and that this performance can potentially be extended to mobile devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a CNN trained with only pixels and labels as inputs achieves a level of performance comparable to that of dermatologists.
a deep neural network trained with only pixels and labels can classify skin cancer at a dermatologist level.
we have demonstrated the ability of deep neural networks to achieve a level of competence for skin cancer classification on par with dermatologists.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single CNN can be trained end to end on a dataset of 2,000 diseases to classify skin cancer.
the performance of a CNN can match or even outperform dermatologists on skin cancer classification tasks.
a single deep convolutional neural network can be trained to classify skin cancer with a performance on par with dermatologists, using only pixels as input.
